strings.name: Lisa Su
strings.role: AMD chair and CEO · High-performance computing
strings.summary: Su trained in electrical engineering and semiconductor research and worked at Texas Instruments, IBM and Freescale. At AMD she led teams developing Ryzen, EPYC and Instinct product lines and expanded into adaptive computing through the Xilinx acquisition, advancing AMD’s role in processor and AI-computing competition.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through November 13, 2026; the timeline includes operating information published that November. Chip development is a team achievement, and a GPU deployment agreement does not mean all facilities are complete.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: MIT: bachelor’s (1990), master’s (1991) and doctorate (1994) in electrical engineering
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Associated organizations
strings.facts.fact-03.value: AMD; previously Texas Instruments, IBM and Freescale
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: High-performance processors
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Led AMD’s introduction of Zen-based Ryzen products and the development of its high-performance processor business.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Broader computing portfolio
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Completed the Xilinx acquisition in 2022, adding adaptive computing to AMD’s business.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: AI computing infrastructure
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: Advanced the Instinct accelerator business and announced a GPU deployment partnership with OpenAI in 2025.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Discusses data-center progress
strings.timeline.event-01.text: As chair and CEO, commented on third-quarter results, emphasizing demand for EPYC and Instinct products.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Announces an OpenAI partnership
strings.timeline.event-02.text: AMD and OpenAI announced a six-gigawatt GPU deployment agreement; that capacity is a phased plan.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Completes Xilinx deal and becomes chair
strings.timeline.event-03.text: AMD completed its Xilinx acquisition; the board elected her chair on the same day.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Ryzen 7 reaches the market
strings.timeline.event-04.text: AMD launched Zen-based Ryzen 7 desktop processors, renewing its challenge in high-performance CPUs.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Becomes AMD CEO
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Promoted from chief operating officer to president and CEO, also joining the board.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Joins AMD
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Became senior vice president and general manager of global business units, overseeing product strategy and execution.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Moves to Freescale
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Became chief technology officer, leading technology roadmaps and research before taking business-management roles.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Joins IBM
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Worked in semiconductor research and management, contributing to chip processes and technology partnerships.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Completes her MIT doctorate
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Earned a doctorate in electrical engineering and then worked in a technical role at Texas Instruments.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Taiwan
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Tainan and moved to the United States with her family as a young child.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced high-performance processors and computing platforms at AMD, influencing semiconductor competition and AI computing infrastructure.
